title: Keerthy Suresh Fires Back at Claims She Took The Paradise Dance Number Due to 'Lack of Roles'
excerpt: The National Award-winning actress responded with a sharp 'chinna correction' after a social media user suggested she accepted the special song in Nani's upcoming film because she lacked substantial roles.
body:
• Keerthy Suresh responded to a social media user who claimed she was doing a special dance number in Nani's The Paradise due to a "lack of substantial roles"
  • The actress dismissed the claim with a witty "chinna correction" (small correction), pointing to her packed slate of upcoming projects
  • Keerthy is currently filming the special song alongside nearly 1,000 dancers on an elaborate Hyderabad set, choreographed by Aata Sandeep

Keerthy Suresh shut down a social media user's claim that she accepted a special dance number in Nani's The Paradise because she lacked "substantial roles," responding with a characteristically sharp "chinna correction" — Telugu for "a small correction."

The exchange, which went viral across Indian social media platforms this week, began when a user commented that the National Award-winning actress was doing the dance number because she had no other significant work. Multiple outlets, including Hindustan Times and NDTV, reported on Keerthy's response, which her fans praised as measured but firm.

A Packed Schedule Says Otherwise

The claim sits awkwardly against Keerthy's actual work calendar. The actress is currently shooting as the female lead opposite Vijay Deverakonda in Rowdy Janardhana, and has been cast alongside Venkatesh in director Anil Ravipudi's upcoming multi-starrer. Earlier this year, she expressed her desire to take on more performance-driven roles similar to her National Award-winning portrayal in Mahanati.

"It wasn't meant to be disrespectful," Keerthy told reporters during a recent promotional appearance, addressing the broader tendency of social media users to question actresses' career choices. Her filmography spans more than 30 films across Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam cinema, and she made her Bollywood debut with Baby John alongside Varun Dhawan.

The Paradise Special Song

The special song that sparked the controversy is itself a major production. According to Telugu Cinema, the track is being filmed on a specially erected set in Hyderabad, featuring nearly 1,000 junior artists and dancers. Popular choreographer Aata Sandeep is overseeing the choreography, with Anirudh Ravichander composing the music.

Reports from Tupaki indicate that Keerthy laid specific conditions before agreeing to the number: the song should be promoted as a "special number" rather than an "item number," and she would review the final edit before its theatrical release. Industry observers noted these conditions reflect her careful approach to her screen image.

"I don't want to rush. I need some time to deliver it."

— Srikanth Odela, Director, The Paradise

Nani-Keerthy Reunion Raises Expectations

The special song marks the third collaboration between Keerthy and Nani, following Nenu Local and the blockbuster Dasara. It is also her second project with director Srikanth Odela, who helmed Dasara. The duo's on-screen chemistry in that 2023 hit was widely praised, and Nani was among the select guests invited to Keerthy's wedding to Antony.

The Paradise, produced by Sudhakar Cherukuri under the SLV Cinemas banner, is being mounted as Nani's biggest pan-India project. The film features the actor as a fierce leader of a marginalized community fighting for citizenship. The ensemble cast includes Kayadu Lohar as the female lead, Raghav Juyal as the antagonist, and Mohan Babu and Sampoornesh Babu in key roles.

What's Next

The Paradise has had a turbulent release schedule, originally set for March 2026 before being pushed to August 21. Recent reports from Pinkvilla suggest a further delay to September 25, with nearly 60 shooting days still remaining as of June. The makers have denied persistent reshoot rumors, stating that over 100 shooting days were completed without any reshoots.

For the Indian diaspora audience, the film's multi-language release — in Telugu, Hindi, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, English, and Spanish — positions it as one of the most accessible South Indian films of the year. The first single, Aaya Sher, composed by Anirudh Ravichander, has already generated buzz ahead of the theatrical release.
nri_angle: Keerthy Suresh is one of the most prominent South Indian actresses with a growing fanbase in the diaspora. The Paradise's multi-language release including English and Spanish makes it one of the most accessible South Indian films globally.
